title: explicit shuts the trap
prompt: Implement `class Meters` with `explicit Meters(double v)` storing `v` privately and `double value() const`. The test proves `Meters m = 3.0;` must NOT compile while `Meters m{3.0};` must — your class needs exactly one `explicit` one-argument constructor.

tests.name: brace-init
tests.hint: Direct initialization with braces works with explicit.

tests.name: copy-list
tests.hint: Copy from an existing object is still allowed.
